docs.title: tempus
docs.text: tempus is a small time tracker that grew from a single Python file into a CLI, an HTTP API and a React dashboard. It is designed to run on one machine, store its data in SQLite or PostgreSQL, and stay out of the way.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• One running timer at a time, with projects and tags.
  • Reports by day, project and arbitrary date range.
  • CSV and JSON export, plus a JSON import path for old backups.
  • Accounts and per-user scoping for the API and dashboard.
  • Prometheus metrics and structured logs.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
$ pip install -e .
$ tempus start "reading the docs" --project tempus
$ tempus stop
$ tempus report --days 1

For the API and dashboard see Deployment.

docs.title: HTTP API
docs.text: Start the API with uvicorn tempus.api.main:app --reload and open /docs for the generated OpenAPI interface.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Path Description GET /health Liveness probe with the package version. GET /api/entries List entries, newest first. POST /api/entries Create an entry. POST /api/entries/start Start a timer, refusing when one is running. POST /api/entries/{id}/stop Stop a timer. PATCH /api/entries/{id} Change the label, project or tags. DELETE /api/entries/{id} Remove an entry. GET /api/projects List active projects. POST /api/projects Create a project. POST /api/projects/{id}/archive Archive a project. GET /api/tags List tag names. GET /api/reports/summary Totals grouped by project and day.

Listing endpoints accept limit and offset. limit is capped at 200 so a sleeping browser tab cannot ask for the entire history at once.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The project is intentionally layered so the same core can serve the CLI today and a small API later.

tempus/
  models.py     dataclasses, no I/O
  storage.py    persistence (JSON and SQLite)
  reports.py    pure aggregation helpers
  export.py     CSV/JSON adapters
  config.py     configuration precedence
  cli.py        argument parsing and presentation

Rules of thumb:

  • models, reports and export must not print or read argv.
  • Storage backends expose all, add, update and delete.
  • The CLI converts exceptions into exit codes; it never raises for user error.

The SQLite schema is deliberately boring. Timestamps are stored as ISO strings in local time so they stay readable when debugging by hand.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The API issues a signed JWT from POST /api/auth/login. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token> on every other request.

  • Passwords are hashed with bcrypt; the plain text never reaches the database.
  • Tokens expire after twelve hours by default (TEMPUS_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES).
  • There is no refresh token yet. The dashboard simply asks you to sign in again.
  • GET /api/auth/me is useful for checking a token without side effects.

The token secret lives in TEMPUS_SECRET_KEY. Rotating it signs everyone out, which is the quickest response to a leaked token.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
Command Description start <label> Start a timer, optionally with --project and --tags. stop Stop the running timer. status Print the running entry. list Show the ten most recent entries. add <label> --duration 1h30m Record an entry after the fact. edit <index> --label ... Change an existing entry. delete <index> Remove an entry. report --days 7 Totals for the last seven days. report --from 2021-05-01 --to 2021-06-01 Totals for a date range. week One line per day. summary --days 7 JSON totals for scripts. export --format csv out.csv Export entries. import out.json Import entries. config Print resolved configuration. migrate Move JSON entries into SQLite.

Exit codes are 0 on success and 1 on user error, so the commands compose well in shell scripts.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
tempus reads an optional INI file from ~/.config/tempus/config.ini.

[storage]
database = /home/me/.tempus.db

[general]
default_project = side-projects
week_starts_on = monday

Environment variables take precedence over the file:

Variable Purpose TEMPUS_DB SQLite database path TEMPUS_FILE Legacy JSON file path TEMPUS_CONFIG Location of the INI file

docs.title: Load testing
docs.text: Load testing follows the same rule everywhere: one canonical representation on disk, formatting only at the edges. A short note on load testing: prefer the documented flags over editing the database by hand. Hand edits are supported but easy to get wrong.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text: Keep caching in mind when writing scripts: the defaults are chosen for interactive use, not for unattended runs. Caching is handled at the boundary. The CLI validates input before anything reaches the storage layer, which keeps the core easy to test.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
The smallest sensible production setup is docker compose with PostgreSQL and a reverse proxy that terminates TLS.

  1. Copy docker-compose.prod.yml and create .env with POSTGRES_PASSWORD and a random TEMPUS_SECRET_KEY.
  2. Start the stack with docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d.
  3. Put the nginx sample from deploy/nginx.conf in front of ports 3000 and 8000.
  4. Schedule deploy/backup.sh daily. It keeps thirty days of dumps.

docs.title: Upgrades
docs.text: Run alembic upgrade head before restarting the API container. The compose command already does this, which is fine for a single node deployment.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: Never ship the default TEMPUS_SECRET_KEY. Rotating it invalidates every issued token, which is the intended way to force a re-login after a leak.

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
The dashboard lives in web/ and is built with Vite, React and TypeScript.

$ cd web
$ npm install
$ npm run dev

Vite proxies /api to http://localhost:8000, so start the API first.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
Path Purpose src/api Typed fetch wrapper and shared types src/hooks Data loading and timer state src/components Presentation only, no fetching src/pages One component per route src/lib Formatting helpers, unit tested with vitest

Components never call fetch directly. That keeps the API boundary in one place when the endpoints change.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
$ python -m venv .venv
$ . .venv/bin/activate
$ pip install -e .

The first time you run tempus, entries are stored in the legacy JSON file. Run tempus migrate once to move them into SQLite.

docs.title: A normal day
docs.text:
$ tempus start "review pull requests" --project tempus --tags review
$ tempus stop
$ tempus today

If you forget to stop a timer, tempus edit lets you fix the label but the end time still has to come from tempus stop. Manual entries are easier:

$ tempus add "writing notes" --duration 45m

docs.title: Where is my data?
docs.text:
• SQLite database: ~/.tempus.db (override with TEMPUS_DB).
  • JSON fallback: ~/.tempus.json (override with TEMPUS_FILE).
  • Config: ~/.config/tempus/config.ini.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
The API exposes two endpoints that are not part of the public schema:

  • GET /health runs a trivial query so a failing database is visible to the load balancer.
  • GET /metrics returns Prometheus text format.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: Metric Labels Meaning tempus_http_requests_total method, status Request counter tempus_http_request_duration_seconds method Latency histogram tempus_timers_started_total — Started timers

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: Set TEMPUS_LOG_JSON=1 to emit one JSON object per line. Every request logs a short request id which is also returned in the x-request-id header, so a browser report can be matched to a server line.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: The rate limiter keeps counters in process memory. With more than one API replica the effective limit multiplies; move the bucket to Redis before scaling out.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text:
1. Run the full suite: pytest in the root and npm test in web/.
  2. Check ruff check tempus tests and npm run lint.
  3. Update CHANGELOG.md and bump tempus/__init__.py.
  4. Run the migrations against a copy of production data.
  5. Tag the release: git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "vX.Y.Z" and push the tag.
  6. Confirm the container image appears in GHCR.
  7. Deploy, then check /health and the dashboard login.
